elements.quote: Among the studies included in this SRMA, six studies were in Amhara, four in SNNP region, two in Oromia, two in Addis Ababa, two in Harari, one in Dire Dawa and two in Tigray. Fourteen of the studies were cross sectional, four were cohort and one case control studies. A total of 8755 participants with the smallest 166 to the largest 1069 participants included and found the prevalence which ranges from 6.80 to 25.4% of SSI following cesarean section in Ethiopia. On the other hand, the quality of each study was assessed by using NOS, the score of all included studies lies between 8 to 9 which indicates good quality.
elements.reason: Briefly summarizes study characteristics (region, design, sample size, prevalence range) and risk of bias (NOS scores) for the included studies contributing to the synthesis.

elements.quote: 19 articles were found eligible for inclusion in the final SRMA (Fig 1). Among the studies included in this SRMA, six studies were in Amhara, four in SNNP region, two in Oromia, two in Addis Ababa, two in Harari, one in Dire Dawa and two in Tigray.
elements.reason: Identifies the number and regional distribution of studies but does not name individual studies explicitly; references Fig 1 which is not provided in evidence.

elements.quote: Subgroup analysis was done by using the study region and the result revealed that the pooled prevalence of SSI cesarean section was highest in Amhara region (12.47%; 95% (CI: 7.33, 17.60%), I 2 = 95.28%, P = 0.00) followed by SNNP region (11.76%; 95% (CI: 10.29, 13.22%), I 2 = 0.00%, P = 0.86). on the contrary, the lowest prevalence of SSI after cesarean section was observed in Tigray region (8.91%; 95%CI: 4.15, 13.66%), I 2 = 72.24%, P = 0.06) followed by Oromia region (9.18%; 95%CI: 7.16, 11.20%), I 2 = 0.00%, P = 0.77 (Fig 4).
elements.reason: Results of subgroup analysis, an investigation of heterogeneity, are reported with estimates, confidence intervals, and heterogeneity statistics (I², p-values).

elements.quote: The result of this SRMA showed the overall pooled prevalence of SSI following cesarean section in Ethiopia was 11.13% with a 95% CI: (9.29, 12.97%), which is much higher than the global prevalence of 5.63% [40]. This result is consistent with a study conducted in Rwanda which is 10.9% [14]. However, this was lower than the study conducted in China [15], Jordan [41] and Ekiti state, Nigeria [13] reported 23.3%, 14.4% and 16.01% respectively.
elements.reason: The authors interpret the pooled prevalence by comparing it with global data and specific studies from other countries, providing context for the results.
